proposals.hypothesis: Alumina-based oxides like LiAlO2 are known to improve cycling stability and form stable interfaces with oxide cathodes, likely offering good insulation and compatibility.
Niobate coatings such as LiNbO3 exhibit high ionic conductivity and electrochemical stability at high voltages, potentially reducing side reactions.
Tantalate analogues like LiTaO3 share similar beneficial properties with niobates, often showing even higher stability and suitable band gaps for insulation.
Zirconates such as Li2ZrO3 can form robust protective layers and may have good compatibility with the LLZO electrolyte due to shared Zr-O bonds.
Phosphate coatings like Li3PO4 are widely studied for their ability to suppress transition metal dissolution and provide stable Li-ion transport.
Silicates like Li2SiO3 may offer good thermal and chemical stability, with silicate frameworks potentially offering tunable ionic conductivity.
Borates such as LiBO2 can form glassy coatings that uniformly cover cathode particles, possibly enhancing rate capability and stability.
Halide coatings like LiF are insulating and can potentially suppress parasitic reactions, though their stability at high voltage is less explored.
Mixed titanium silicates like Li2TiSiO5 may combine the stability of titanates and silicates, potentially offering a balanced interface.
Aluminosilicates like LiAlSiO4 are structurally stable and may provide good adhesion and insulation due to their framework structure.
